newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Everbright Int'l announces assets sales.
newsitem.headline: Everbright Int'l announces assets sales.

text.p: China Everbright International Ltd will sell its 55 percent interest in a China-based pipe manufacturer, the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
The company is also selling one commercial property and is in the process of buying another, the statement said.

The company did not have any plans to acquire the 7.74 percent shareholding in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd recently acquired by its parent company China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd, the annnouncement said.
The statement said Everbright International would dispose of its entire 55 percent holding in Hebei Xinxing Pipes Co Ltd for a consideration of HK$142 million, the statement said.
The consideration represented the company's cost of investment and shareholders' loans (plus interest accrued at 6.5 percent per annum) advanced to Xinxing Pipes, it said.
The Xinxing Pipes' disposal would result in a profit of approximately HK$15 million if completed, the statement said.
The company also announced that it had sold the entire eighth floor of Lippo Tower in Lippo Centre for a total consideration of HK$199.53 million.

The proceeds would be used as general working capital and to finance the acquisition of another commercial property, currently partly leased by the company and partly by sister company China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd, it said.
The company's operating strategy is to substantiate and diversity its earnings base by capitalising on investment opportunities in major industrial enterprises in China, it said.

Based on 1.6 billion shares in issue, the net asset value of the company was about HK$0.92 per share, which represented about 43.3 percent of the closing price of HK$2.125 per share on May 26, the statement said.
The company's 1996 earnings per share was HK$0.27, putting the share on a price/earnings ratio of 787 times, it added.

The share price of Everbright International had risen 46.6 percent since April 1, 1997, and the rise was neither backed by a corresponding increase in the asset backing of the company, nor by any improvement on profitability of its existing, it said.
Trading in the shares, which was suspended on May 27, resumed on Tuesday, the announcement said.
The shares were trading HK$0.225 higher at HK$2.35 in early trade.
